title: Argument relations (AIF core)
description: LLM output format for classifying relations between a flat set of already-extracted arguments/claims, each identified by an integer id. Models only the AIF core (I/RA/CA nodes; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument_Interchange_Format and the official schema at https://www.arg.tech/wp-content/uploads/AIF.sql): a relation is itself the object (an 'RA-node' for support, a 'CA-node' for conflict), not a labelled edge -- this naturally covers coordinative groups (several arguments jointly backing one claim), which a flat from/to edge cannot express. Deliberately without the AIF+ dialogue layer (L/YA/TA nodes, locutions, illocutionary acts): this schema assumes arguments have already been extracted as clean, standalone claims, not raw dialogue turns -- suitable for any pipeline that has arguments/claims as rows/objects with an id, not specific to any one project's database.

relations.description: All relations found between the supplied arguments. Empty array if none were found -- never omit the field or force a relation that isn't really there.

relation.description: One RA-node (support) or CA-node (conflict): premise_argument_ids feed the relation, target_argument_id is the argument being supported or attacked.

relation_type.description: support = RA-node (premises logically back up the target). conflict = CA-node (premises rebut or undermine the target).

target_argument_id.description: id of the argument (I-node) being supported or attacked.

premise_argument_ids.description: id's of the arguments (I-nodes) that feed the relation. More than 1 item = a coordinative group: the premises only carry the target jointly, not individually.

scheme.description: Refinement of relation_type, analogous to AIF's schemes table (a named argumentation scheme applied by this relation). For conflict: 'direct_rebuttal' (explicitly rebuts the same point), 'thematic' (touches the same sub-topic, no direct rebuttal), or 'frame_shift' (shifts the discussion to a different value/framing instead of rebutting the point itself). For support: a Walton argumentation-scheme name (e.g. 'Argument from Cause to Effect', 'Argument from Expert Opinion') if one clearly applies, otherwise null -- never guess a scheme that doesn't fit.

weak_link.description: true if the premise does not actually logically support/rebut the target despite being structurally or topically close to it (e.g. two arguments placed near each other that don't really engage with the same point) -- flags a relation that looks plausible on the surface but doesn't hold up.

confidence.description: Model's confidence in this relation, 0.0-1.0. Not a probability in a strict statistical sense -- a self-reported certainty estimate.
